Name: engineering-ssh
Description: Engineers may open a shell on the web and database tiers
Purpose: The ordinary rule: a group, two host groups, a service group; the SELinux map hangs off it

Name: staff-bastion
Description: Everyone on staff may reach the jump host
Purpose: The broadest grant, through the root of the nesting chain, to a host that demands a second factor

Name: finance-payroll
Description: Finance may use payroll on the database host
Purpose: One user admitted twice, by name and by group; a report that counts grants gets two

Name: contractors-kiosk
Description: Contractors may log in at the reception kiosk
Purpose: Contractors reach exactly one host and only at the console

Name: legacy-open-door
Purpose: An allow-everything rule that is switched off, which an audit must still list

Name: unbound
Description: A rule that names nobody and nothing
Purpose: Enabled and empty: it grants nothing and looks like a mistake

Name: offboarding-leftover
Description: Left behind when an account was disabled
Purpose: A disabled user still named in a rule; the grant is dormant, not gone
